plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (winner pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Bidding above value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a one-shot game with no repeated learning needed, the optimal action is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $30.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid, so there's no benefit to shading my bid down, and bidding above my value risks winning at a price exceeding my value. With a private value of $35, my optimal action is to bid exactly $35, ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding exactly my value of $6 maximizes my expected profit: if others bid less, I win and pay less than my value (profit); if others bid more, I lose but avoid overpaying. This holds true for a single round with no repeated game considerations affecting strategy.
